A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IMPACT framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–B are readable and support comparison despite reformatting and additions.

before.justification: v2 reports original compression experiments on mathematical reasoning and code generation, including accuracy, quantization, throughput, and memory results.

after.justification: v4 reports IMPACT experiments and additional ablation, importance-matrix, and profiling results. Attribution of some baseline scores to other work does not negate these original results.

M1.justification: The objective, gradient-weighted covariance, eigenvector selection, keeping-ratio rule, and compressed weight and bias construction remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithm 1. Expanded derivations and implementation disclosures do not introduce a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate mathematical reasoning on GSM8K/MATH and code generation on HumanEval/MBPP. v4 names MetaMathQA-395K and Code-Instructions-120K as calibration sources for these existing experiments; it does not establish that calibration coverage was added or replaced.

E2.justification: ASVD moves from citation-only coverage in v2 to evaluated comparisons across all four benchmarks in v4 Figures 2–5 and Tables 6–9. Quantization comparisons also add 8-bit AFM in Tables 1–2. These substantially expand the relevant controls. ASVD is mentioned in Section 4.5 but is absent from the corresponding inference Figure 8 and Table 14.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce an η sweep over 0, 0.25, 0.5, and 0.75 at keeping ratios of 50%, 60%, and 70%, and a single-A100 profiling-cost comparison. Existing evaluation tasks, model families, Pass@1 metric, and pre/post-compression finetuning sequence remain. Newly specified optimizer and calibration settings do not establish changes to earlier protocols.

E4.justification: v4 adds four-layer importance-matrix heatmaps and distributions in Appendix B.1, plus the η sensitivity study in B.2; neither analysis appears in v2. B.3 additionally reports calibration-size convergence qualitatively, without a detailed sweep. These substantially extend the mechanism and sensitivity evidence beyond the retained gradient-magnitude illustration.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty across repeated evaluations. The new importance-matrix histograms and quantiles describe matrix entries rather than experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: Many IMPACT/AFM size–accuracy entries are replaced, alongside new comparator and analysis results. Uncompressed CodeLlama HumanEval scores change from 36.0% to 45.1% for 7B and 45.7% to 52.4% for 13B (v2 Tables 6–7; v4 Tables 8–9). Maximum reported Llama 2-7B GSM8K size reduction changes from 48.6% to 55.4%, while CodeLlama-7B HumanEval reduction changes from 48.9% to 24.2%. These are revised reports, not established same-setting gains; compression points and comparator membership also change.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 corrects the QM–AM equality condition. A.2 revises the bounding argument through absolute component products and QM–AM before approximately factorizing the expectation of squared terms, replacing v2's earlier mean-product step. The theorem statements and closed-form solution remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion strengthen the quantitative compression claim from up to 48.6% to 55.4% greater size reduction. The principal novelty claim and contribution of performance-aware activation reconstruction through a weighted-covariance eigensolution remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly interprets long-tailed importance values as emphasizing rare critical interactions, explains profiling overhead through backward passes and ASVD rank search, and explicitly states calibration-distribution dependence alongside architecture-generic applicability. These add substantive explanations and qualifications to the retained interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 gives little experimental implementation information. v4 Section 4.1 and Appendix B.3 disclose calibration datasets and fractions, AdamW learning rates, cosine scheduling, warmup, BF16, FSDP, batch sizes, GPU allocation, and profiling hardware/cost. These substantially improve reproducibility documentation without establishing that the previously used settings changed.

R1.justification: v4 adds calibration-data references, sensitivity-based pruning references supporting Taylor approximations, and brief discussion of trustworthiness, structured pruning, and token compression. It also identifies Li et al. (2025a) as the source of several baseline results. The central positioning and claimed novelty remain intact.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten, local explanations and cross-references are refined, and Appendix B gains four named subsections. Affiliations, publication information, Limitations, and Acknowledgments are added. The main section sequence and much of the existing prose remain.

P2.justification: v4 adds Figures 9–10 and ablation, profiling-cost, and throughput tables; redraws comparison plots with expanded legends and changed HumanEval axes; and moves the 13B quantization figure into the main text. v2 Tables 4–7 are split into performance Tables 6–9 and reduction Tables 10–13. Page format, typography, and table placement also change substantially.

improvement.justification: The added ASVD and 8-bit AFM controls, η ablation, profiling evidence, and calibration/SFT details strengthen empirical support and reproducibility. However, the central theoretical guarantee remains unresolved: Appendix A.2 still uses Taylor truncation and an approximate expectation factorization while asserting an exact upper bound. v4 therefore offers useful supporting evidence and transparency gains without repairing that core deficiency.
